name: Possibility space

subjectOf.text: The computative agent is not a satisficer, because computational resources are capital rather than a fixed cognitive endowment, so added capacity scales the size and quality of the generable possibility space rather than easing a cognitive bound.
subjectOf.abstract: The computative agent is not a satisficer. Computational resources are capital rather than a fixed cognitive endowment. An increase in computational capacity increases the size and quality of the possibility space the agent can generate
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Computative Economics A Framework for Economic Analysis under Computational Abundance (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6607458

subjectOf.text: In Neoclassical analysis the action space is a parameter of the model and the agent is a chooser within it, whereas in Computative Economics the action space is an output of the agent and the agent is a generator over it; every operational difference between the two architectures follows from this parameter versus output distinction.
subjectOf.abstract: in Neoclassical analysis, the action space is a parameter of the model and the agent is a chooser within it. In Computative Economics analysis, the action space is an output of the agent and the agent is a generator over it.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Possibility Loops An Operational Architecture for Computative Economics in Agent Coordination Systems (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6655138

subjectOf.text: An architecture with a reward channel but no action surface implements generation as an off-protocol act whose outputs cannot enter the protocol's action set, so the protocol's possibility space remains exogenous no matter how generatively active the agent population is.
subjectOf.abstract: An architecture that has the reward channel but no action surface implements G as an off-protocol act whose outputs cannot enter the protocol's action set, and the protocol's possibility space remains exogenous regardless of how active G is in the agent population.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Possibility Loops An Operational Architecture for Computative Economics in Agent Coordination Systems (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6655138
scope_conditions: protocols lacking a settlement-layer interface for posting generative output

subjectOf.text: Without a representation of the possibility space distinct from the current mempool of pending instances, no quality metric can be computed, and without quality metrics generation can be rewarded only for quantity and not for quality.
subjectOf.abstract: Without that representation, no quality metric can be computed, and without quality metrics, generation cannot be rewarded for quality, only for quantity.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Possibility Loops An Operational Architecture for Computative Economics in Agent Coordination Systems (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=6655138
scope_conditions: architectures whose only action-space representation is pending or executing instances
